nucleus.thesis: The disagreement assumes 'freely distributed' means 'uniformly distributed to all actors.' Reframe: freedom of the model itself (open code) is independent from freedom of access to specific instantiations (graduated deployment tiers).
nucleus.why_not_blend: Both Spirits' non-negotiables—Boolean's friction/verification AND Roux's transparency/openness—become compatible once we stop treating 'distribution' as a binary switch and instead separate source-code openness from deployment-access granularity.

claims.text: Open-source weights (transparency, auditability, distributed knowledge) can coexist with tiered deployment access (institutional review for high-risk variants) without betraying either principle.
The real variable isn't whether open code exists, but whether capability *concentration* (which actor deploys what, at what scale) remains distributed or monopolized.
Accountability registries and deployment-cost mechanisms (Boolean's 'friction') create incentives that make perfect enforcement unnecessary while preserving Roux's radical transparency.
Misuse detectability (Roux's key insight) is maximized by open weights + observable deployment patterns, not by open weights alone or closed systems.

shell.topic: Should open-source AI models be freely distributed?

adjacency.target: biosafety-style institutional review adapted to AI
binary open/closed framing into: transparency layer vs. access control layer
